findings.title: Team admin/owner permission check uses `&&` instead of `||`
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0))`. Because it uses `&&` rather than `||`, a user must satisfy both `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` simultaneously. A team admin who is not the team owner (or any user if `isTeamAdmin` only matches the `ADMIN` role) will fail authorization with `FORBIDDEN` when trying to add guests to a team booking.

findings.title: `EventManager` is initialized with the caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
findings.body: `addGuestsHandler` allows team admins/owners and attendees (in addition to the organizer) to add guests to a booking, and fetches `booking.user` with `credentials` and `destinationCalendar` in the initial query. However, lines 158-165 fetch credentials for `ctx.user` and initialize `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` using the logged-in caller rather than `booking.user`. When an attendee or team admin adds guests, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will attempt to update the organizer's calendar event using the caller's credentials, failing to update the organizer's calendar.

findings.title: Guest email filtering is case-sensitive, does not deduplicate input, and `sendAddGuestsEmails` receives unfiltered `guests`
findings.body:
There are three issues with how `guests` is filtered and used:
1. `blacklistedGuestEmails` lowercases entries on line 71, but `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` and `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` compare against `guest` without lowercasing it, allowing mixed-case emails to bypass both the blacklist and existing-attendee checks.
2. Neither `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` nor `uniqueGuests` deduplicates the `guests` array itself, so duplicate emails in a direct API call will insert duplicate attendee rows.
3. Line 168 calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw `guests` array instead of `uniqueGuests`. If the input included an already-existing attendee email alongside a new one, that existing attendee will match `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` and receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`.

findings.title: `isInvalidEmail` error state is not cleared on valid submission or dialog close
findings.body: Once `setIsInvalidEmail(true)` is triggered by a validation failure, `isInvalidEmail` is only ever reset if the user clicks the Cancel button. It is not reset when validation succeeds in `handleAdd`, in `addGuestsMutation.onSuccess`, or when the dialog is dismissed via `onOpenChange` (Escape key or backdrop click). As a result, the invalid email warning remains visible during the mutation and persists if the dialog is reopened.

findings.title: `sendAddGuestsEmails` ignores `disableStandardEmails` event type metadata settings
findings.body: Unlike `sendScheduledEmails`, `sendRescheduledEmails`, and `sendLocationChangeEmails`, `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not accept `eventTypeMetadata` or check `eventTypeDisableHostEmail(eventTypeMetadata)` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail(eventTypeMetadata)`. Event types configured with `metadata.disableStandardEmails.all.host` or `metadata.disableStandardEmails.all.attendee` will still send emails to the organizer, team members, and attendees when guests are added.
